subject: SoleTerra Coupa invite blocked by email panel sanitizer - PO on hold
messages: From: Alex Romero To: Irene Choi Cc: procurement@soleterra.com Date: 2026-05-17T09:12:00-07:00 Subject: Coupa invite - accept button disappears in Apple Mail Hi Irene, We received the supplier invite email this morning but the big accept button is not visible in Apple Mail (macOS 12). The message shows the Redwood logo panel but no actionable accept link — only a faint plain-text URL that appears truncated when clicked. Procurement has put the PO on hold until we can accept the portal invite. I attached a screenshot of the message and I can forward the original mail if helpful. What quick workaround can we use so SoleTerra can claim the vendor account and pull the PO? Thanks, Alex Alex Romero SoleTerra Procurement Procurement Lead From: Irene Choi To: Ben Carter , Laura Bennett Cc: Alex Romero , procurement@soleterra.com Date: 2026-05-17T10:03:00-07:00 Subject: Re: Coupa invite - accept button disappears in Apple Mail Ben / Laura — raising a potential incident. Alex reports the invite renders with an image-heavy header and the accept CTA is inside an email "panel" that our HTML sanitizer (and/or Apple Mail) is stripping, leaving only a broken/shortened link. Procurement won't accept the PO until the supplier can onboard. Quick context: - Account: SoleTerra Manufacturing, PO #ST-4421 (hold) - Invite id: abc123 (Coupa invite URL included in original) - Observed client: Apple Mail on macOS; internal preview in Gmail showed the CTA but the raw message has an panel with an embedded an href overlay that some clients remove when images are blocked. Immediate asks: 1) Ben — can you check the invite template pipeline (email render service) to see if the accept CTA is encoded as an image map/overlay instead of a clear anchor text? If so, we should fallback to a visible text link at top of message. 2) Laura — please prepare a one-click manual claim link (temporary token route) we can send to Alex that bypasses the rendered CTA. Also include a plain-text claim code and step-by-step instructions. 3) Alex — if you can forward the original mail (raw), attach it so we can inspect headers (spam/stripper) — I attached the screenshot to this thread. I'll keep procurement updated. If this is a template regression we may need a fast rollback of the last email template push. Thanks, Irene Choi Sr. Partnerships Redwood Inference From: Ben Carter To: Irene Choi , Laura Bennett Cc: Alex Romero Date: 2026-05-17T11:28:00-07:00 Subject: Re: Coupa invite - accept button disappears in Apple Mail Thanks Irene — I dug into the outbound render logs. The invite CTA was rendered as a responsive image panel with an absolute-positioned anchor overlaid (we believed this was safe). Two problems I see: 1) some mail clients convert image overlay anchors into inaccessible elements when images are suppressed; 2) our HTML minifier rewrote a long tracking parameter and the shortener produced a 301 that some clients render as a plain text line (leading to truncation). Workarounds I can push now: - Generate a manual claim URL that uses the invite token (no tracker params) and send in plain text. - Also create a 6-digit claim code that the supplier can paste into a short form on the Coupa claim flow (we'll add this helper endpoint). I'll create the manual-link and code in the next 20 minutes and share in reply. If this recurs we'll revert the overlay CTA change and force a text-first CTA. Attaching: raw-invite.eml for header inspection and a screenshot. -Ben Ben Carter Platform Ops Redwood Inference From: Irene Choi To: Alex Romero , procurement@soleterra.com Cc: Ben Carter , Laura Bennett Date: 2026-05-18T15:04:00-07:00 Subject: Re: Coupa invite - accept button disappears in Apple Mail Alex — quick update and manual route to unblock the PO: Manual claim link (works regardless of client sanitizers): https://coupa.com/invite/abc123?manual=true One-time claim code: 742915 Instructions: 1) Open the link above in any browser (copy-paste if clicking from Apple Mail fails). 2) If the page prompts for a claim code, enter 742915 and your company email. 3) If you hit a sign-in screen, choose "Claim account" — the manual flag bypasses the image-panel flow. We've also scheduled a rollback of the overlay CTA in the next template deploy and will force a visible text link in the header. Laura — please publish the rollback note and a short KB article for suppliers experiencing image-stripping. Once you confirm account claim I will ask CS to remove the PO hold on ST-4421. Sorry for the friction — appreciate the quick flag. Best, Irene Choi Sr. Partnerships, Redwood Inference
